evidence: Figure 1 shows the thickness of a Pt film deposited at 300 °C (reactor wall temperature is 70 °C) as a function of the number of cycles as monitored by in situ spectroscopic ellipsometry. Rutherford backscattering spectrometry revealed that (3.0±0.2)×1014 cm−2 Pt atoms, corresponding to 0.2 ML Pt, are deposited per cycle. The formation of CO2 during both the (MeCp)PtMe3 and O2 pulses can clearly be observed from the absorbance peaks around 2360 cm−1, with most of the CO2 being produced during the O2 pulse. The spectra in Fig. 2 correspond with a total (MeCp)PtMe3 dosing time of 4 s. The data were also compared with a saturation curve measured by spectroscopic ellipsometry at the 300 °C heated substrate holder.
